chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Father's barber shops and the family's first homes in Los Angeles
summary: His father barbered in Dallas and on South Main Street in Los Angeles; the family lived on West Temple then at 417 South Central Avenue.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. And the...your father in Dallas, you said he was a barber--had a barber shop and a general store. Is that right?
He had a barber shop, and my mother and other people ran the store, and he had a barber shop in the Grand Windsor Hotel in Dallas.
And then, when you got to Los Angeles, he was a...he worked as a barber here, too?
Yeah, he had a barber shop on 230 South Main Street.
Whereabouts did you live when you first got here?

When I first lived...came here, we stayed out in...on West Temple Street for a short while, you know, and then we moved to Fourth and Central--417 South Central Avenue. 'Course, that was right in town, almost. And Bekins [Van & Storage] was at Fourth and Alameda so I went to school with the kids. Bekins Van and Storage Company.
